raw.assessment: The scheduled CSV workflow already produces intended course sets in 32/40 exports. The seven-minute median for unchanged assignments is a concrete limiting observation against a universally cumbersome workflow; it does not establish that assignment changes cause the overall 17-minute median. Six affected exports coincide with reassignment and two with renaming, making temporal selection or name reconciliation plausible hypotheses. Execution lasts seconds while replacements take much longer, suggesting delay outside computation without identifying its cause. Observed isolation covers only the sampled files; the omitted split-course center limits that evidence. Spreadsheet actions and timetable accuracy remain unobserved.

openings.claim: Current instructor assignments may select the wrong courses for a historical week; renames may separately make correctly included courses appear absent during name-based checking.
openings.delta: Distinguish actual course omission from identity-label disagreement before changing export logic.
openings.prediction: With expected course membership fixed independently, reassignment changes selected membership, whereas a rename may preserve membership but change coordinators' judgments. Absence of both effects would weaken this account.
openings.probe: In private fabricated staging, compare unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures for the same week. Compare documented CSV contents against predefined expected memberships and have coordinators check files against matched timetables. Include another-center sentinel records and concurrent attendance entry.
assumptions: Expected course membership can be specified independently of current assignments.
The fixture study fits the six-day allowance and existing hosting.

openings.claim: Would immediate authorized regeneration reduce coordinator handling, or mostly reduce elapsed waiting while checking and import work persist?
openings.delta: Separate replacement turnaround from the active-time success measure.
openings.prediction: If repeated status checking and requests dominate, immediate replacement reduces active minutes; if timetable reconciliation or spreadsheet work dominates, turnaround improves with little handling reduction.
openings.probe: Use consenting coordinators' paired short sessions with fabricated files, counterbalanced scenarios and private engineer-assisted immediate replacement. Time checking, requesting, downloading and importing separately; record elapsed wait separately. Preserve the documented schema.
assumptions: Participants can reproduce ordinary checking with fabricated schedules.
The paired study shares the six-day budget with the fixture study.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames coincide with six and two affected exports, respectively; causation is unproved. Two analogies suggest separable selection and delay hypotheses. Neither demonstrates the six-day limit or next-40-export targets.

openings.claim: Adapt manufacturing kits: stable part numbers and a dated bill of materials become center-scoped course identities and a requested-week manifest, checked before CSV assembly. Names and current instructors become attributes rather than selection keys.
openings.delta: Failed correspondence: course splits need a predecessor/successor decision; they are not simple relabeling. Changed material assumptions: identities and historical membership must be recoverable, or coordinators must confirm membership privately. The manifest must not freeze attendance entry.
openings.prediction: If mutable selection attributes explain defects, a confirmed week manifest will reduce omissions after reassignment or renaming; split courses may remain ambiguous. Confirmation effort could erase the time benefit.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, compare existing selection with dated manifests for reassigned, renamed, unchanged, and split courses. Six coordinators identify intended sets and time confirmation. Inspect tenant isolation while attendance entry continues. Retain the documented CSV; estimate implementation effort before selecting the change.
assumptions: Historical membership can be recovered or confirmed within the handling-time target.
Manifest creation and scoped selection fit six engineer-days and existing hosting.

openings.claim: Could a private export pickup counter remove replacement waiting, as a parcel locker separates collection from staff availability? Map authenticated center/week requests to job receipts and retrievable CSVs.
openings.delta: Failed correspondence: a ready parcel is already correct; a completed export can contain wrong courses. Changed material assumptions: coordinators can request replacements without staff intervention, and repeat demand is affordable.
openings.prediction: If staff handoff dominates delay, direct retrieval shortens request-to-download time while leaving course accuracy unchanged; active handling time may barely change.
openings.probe: During the two short sessions, compare assisted and direct replacement requests using fabricated files. Measure request-to-start, execution, download, checking, and import separately; observe concurrent attendance entry and reject cross-center retrieval attempts.
assumptions: Existing authentication and scheduling permit a small center-scoped retrieval flow within six days.
Replacement demand stays within hosting capacity; CSV schema remains supported.

openings.claim: Reassignment may alter historical membership; renames may only confuse checking. Stable center-scoped identities and dated manifests could help; splits require predecessor/successor decisions.
openings.discriminator: Fix expected membership independently: distinguish omitted courses from changed labels and coordinator judgments.
openings.fit: Uncertain: retain private processing, CSV schema and concurrent attendance; verify history recovery, confirmation cost and six-day/hosting feasibility.
openings.probe: Compare existing selection and manifests in private fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split fixtures. Six coordinators check matched timetables and time confirmation; include other-center sentinels and attendance entry.
openings.uncertainty: Associations are not causes; timetables may be incomplete. History may require private confirmation that erases savings; sampled isolation excludes splits.

openings.claim: Immediate replacement or authenticated center/week pickup with receipts and retrievable CSVs may remove staff delay; course correctness remains separate.
openings.discriminator: Reduced status checking/requests lowers active minutes; faster turnaround alone may leave reconciliation/import work unchanged.
openings.fit: Uncertain: preserve privacy, CSV and attendance; authentication, scheduling and repeated demand must fit six days and hosting.
openings.probe: Use two counterbalanced short sessions with fabricated files: compare assisted/direct requests and immediate replacement. Separate request-to-start, execution, elapsed wait, checking, requesting, downloading and importing; test cross-center retrieval rejection and concurrent entry.
openings.uncertainty: Delay source and spreadsheet actions are unobserved; fabricated sessions may not reproduce ordinary work.

lineage.reason: With A1; preserves omission versus label disagreement.
With Z1; retains dated manifests, split ambiguity and confirmation cost.
With A2; retains active-time versus waiting distinction.
With Z2; retains pickup mechanism, authorization and demand assumptions.

post_distill.decision: Prioritize discriminating probes within one shared six-day budget before implementation. No success established: next 40 exports must reach median handling <=12 minutes, intended sets >=95%, and zero foreign-center records.
